title: Do factor-formula AST tokens predict backtest failure (AUROC >= 0.80)?
content: On a synthetic factor-formula set (n=1200, fail-rate 60%, time-ordered split), a bag-of-AST-tokens LogisticRegression predicts backtest FAILURE on the val split with AUROC=0.810 (bar 0.80 -> GO) and recall=0.72 at FPR<=20% (target 0.80). Signal PRESENT: token-visible failure modes (lookahead / undefined fields / malformed arity) are learnable and generalise across the time split, so a light world-model pre-screen has a real basis — proceed to Phase 1 (build the real search->backtest pipeline, measure budget efficiency). The ~30% token-invisible runtime failures cap recall, quantifying the irreducible miss rate.

title: Does the VaR constraint hold tail risk near target on val (robust ≤6%, MVO worse)?
content: Phase-0 refuted (pipeline ran end-to-end; CVaR LP feasible, infeasible_rate=0.0 → the robust optimizer genuinely ran, not a fallback). On val 2021-2022 the CVaR-constrained robust portfolio was RISKIER out-of-sample than plain MVO: 21.7% vs 17.4% of months breached −8% (target ≤6%). Cause: the minimal historical-bootstrap scenario generator underestimates the OOS tail, so 'constrain-tail-then-maximize-return' chases return up to a mis-estimated limit and gets hit in the 2022 regime shift — exactly the gap's own flagged risk (scenario misspecification / non-stationarity). MVO's variance penalty incidentally controls the tail better. The conformal-robustness→VaR transfer is NOT viable in this minimal form; the brief's GARCH/conditional scenario generator is a prerequisite, not optional.

title: Is a flexible pricing model's OOS edge a momentum/vol shortcut, or genuine fundamentals?
content: REAL findata panel (297 SPY+IJH+IJR names, monthly 2012-22; fundamentals coverage 96% built from income/balance statements: size=log assets, value=EPS/price, quality=ROE). VAL: full-model rank-IC 0.057, momentum/vol/reversal = 69% of attribution, BUT fundamentals-only model = 0.085 > full → the model OVER-relies on momentum/vol yet that is NOT its edge; fundamentals carry more signal. So 'the edge is a momentum/vol shortcut' is REFUTED (opposite). HOLDOUT 2021-22: full IC -0.041, fundamentals-only ~-0.045 — both negative, nothing generalizes (regime break). Twofold finding: (1) momentum/vol is not the edge source; (2) no ML stock-prediction edge survives OOS here.

content: Controlled GBM testbed (4 assets, REINFORCE, linear-Gaussian policy). Phase-0 passed (mean per-step reward >0 -> the length-bias driver is present). title: [VALIDATION-CORRECTED] Does decompose→verify-evidence→refuse beat fixed-k retrieval on evidence-grounded answers + refusing on missing data?
content: CORRECTED after E1+E2 validation (evidence-sufficiency-ABLATION). The original +0.64 'confirmed' was an ARTIFACT of (1) deterministic compute and (2) a baseline that couldn't abstain. De-inflated (LLM computes answers; 'unknown'=refusal so baseline can abstain): holdout supported rate baseline 0.60 → decompose-only 0.64 → full 0.64. Total lift +0.04, 95% CI [-0.08,+0.16] (spans 0 → NOT significant). Attribution: decompose +0.04, explicit-refuse +0.00. Answerable accuracy baseline 0.60 > full 0.55 (decomposition does not help answering; LLM arithmetic ~55-60% is the real bottleneck). Residual: full refuses 100% of missing-data vs baseline 60%, but OVER-refuses on answerable (0.35 vs 0.30) so the net washes out. VERDICT: the mechanism's benefit does NOT survive a fair test.

title: E5: does decomposition gather more complete evidence on COMPLEX multi-evidence queries?
content: PRE-REGISTERED validation (peer-median + multi-hop, 30 complex queries, generous baseline fetch budget; primary metric = evidence-completeness, separate from answer accuracy). Result: evidence-completeness baseline 1.00 vs decompose 1.00, GAP +0.00 (CI [0,0]) → REFUTED per pre-registered bar. On structured findata, ad-hoc 'list the fields I need' and explicit decomposition are the same operation, so decomposition adds nothing to evidence-gathering even on 12-field queries. Secondary: answer accuracy BOTH 0.13 — with COMPLETE evidence the LLM computes median/conjunction comparisons right only 13% of the time. SETTLED READ of the whole arc: decompose→verify→refuse gives ~0 measurable benefit on everything testable (simple +0.04 CI spans 0; complex +0.00); the binding constraint is LLM financial REASONING (~13% on complex), which this gap does not address. Untested sliver: real SEC-TEXT retrieval (the proxy can't test it) — but the 13% reasoning ceiling looms over any version. Recommendation: stop.

title: Does the LLM's economic prior buy OOS factor survival that blind search (GP) doesn't?
content: REFUTED on two layers (enriched 15-feat panel 2021-26, deepseek). (1) Economic prior adds nothing: C2 same-model ablation econ vs blind (opaque v1..v15) coef -0.005 t=-1.1 n.s.; blind beats GP as much as econ (C3 +0.0075). (2) The apparent LLM>GP edge is a FORMULA-COMPLEXITY confound: GP mines depth-37 overfit trees, LLM depth-4; at matched IS-IC the simpler formulas survive better (Occam). Depth-matching GP (<=6) REVERSES it (econ vs gp -0.008 t=-2.9). Distilled: LLM-vs-GP must match formula complexity, not just IS-IC; economic-prior claims need the econ-vs-blind same-model ablation.
